extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in the Guttenberg plagiarism case and academic misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarising the 2011 Karl-Theodor zu Guttenberg plagiarism scandal, the university commission's findings, legal/procedural consequences, and the standards and definitions used to judge academic misconduct in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria of academic misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission defined the criteria of academic misconduct as: deliberately or grossly negligent use of misrepresentations (Falschangaben), the violation of intellectual property of others, and the obstruction of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report further defined terms: 'Falschangaben' as fabrication or distortion of data, and 'obstruction of research' as unauthorized use of material with arrogation of its authorship. These definitions formed the baseline for the commission's evaluation of the dissertation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic rules of citations / citation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing citations and violations of the academic rules of citations (including verbatim forms of plagiarism and plagiarism with regard to content where the use of other authors' material was not clearly expressed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: verbatim text elements used without citation; marginal text changes lacking proper citation; citing sources only in the bibliography without clear in-text attribution. The commission treated such practices as violations and as misleading regarding authorship of passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbatim copying and marginal text changes as problematic
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of verbatim text elements and the use with marginal text changes lacking proper citation were evaluated as forms of plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission exemplified this on PRS papers, listing passages, text modifications and extensions; it judged marginal edits plus omission of attribution as attempts to cover up source origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern of creation / indicators of deliberate deception
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission identified a 'pattern of creation' (werkprägendes Bearbeitungsmuster) and judged the number and pattern of citation violations as evidence of intentional deception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated instances, text modifications to conceal origin, and the overall pattern across the dissertation led the commission to conclude intentional actions rather than isolated errors; critics disputed whether such minor changes necessarily indicate intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Parliamentary Research Service (PRS) papers requires prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any publication of PRS papers requires prior approval by the German Bundestag's departmental management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documented that several PRS papers were used without proper citation or prior approval; two PRS papers lacked any citation and others were cited insufficiently, leading to misconceptions about authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisors' and university due diligence / oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors' omission to ask for PRS papers cited in the bibliography and the awarding/grading process (summa cum laude) were subject to criticism as failures of oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission denied responsibility of supervisors for detecting plagiarism based on available indicators, but still criticized their omission to check certain sources and the high grade awarded; critics argued the university's initial awarding and oversight procedures warranted scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of degree as remedy for nonconformity to academic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctoral commission revoked Guttenberg's doctoral degree on grounds that he 'objectively not conformed' to academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The university noted a fast revocation was possible because Guttenberg requested withdrawal of his title; the commission's revocation did not make a formal judgment on intent in some statements, which drew criticism about process and thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal/copyright evaluation threshold and prosecutorial outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution in Hof found prosecutable copyright violations (23 instances) but estimated marginal material damage and discontinued criminal proceedings on condition of a €20,000 charitable payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prosecutor distinguished criminal copyright violations from academic misconduct; the decision to discontinue proceedings was criticized as biased toward economic criteria. The prosecution concluded there was no clear intentional deception and characterized the mental state as at most contingent intent (dolus eventualis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of ghostwriting
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission explicitly noted there were no indications that the dissertation had been written by a ghostwriter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of evidence for ghostwriting was taken into account; the commission evaluated authorship-related indicators separately from citation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral examination (rigorosum) performance does not negate citation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission observed that Guttenberg's 'exceedingly convincing' oral examination performance did not absolve the dissertation of citation violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good performance in oral defense was acknowledged but the commission still judged the written work on citation and authorship criteria independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourced documentation as a detection method (GuttenPlag / VroniPlag)
rubrics_metrics.description: GuttenPlag (a crowdsourced platform) documented unattributed work in the dissertation and served as a source for identifying problematic passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes that GuttenPlag's analyses spurred further investigation and the creation of VroniPlag; critics later accused such platforms of partisanship, but they demonstrated a method by which communities can identify and mark suspected plagiarism fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate over minor text changes as normal editing vs. indicators of cheating
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics argued that multiple instances of minor text changes (which the commission viewed as indicators of cheating) could be typical editorial procedure by an author for their own text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents a contested evaluative principle: whether small textual modifications, when combined with missing citations, reasonably indicate deliberate plagiarism or instead reflect ordinary revision practices.
